the expression of bFgf is increased in CA1 pyramical cells and dentate gyrus granule cells after ischemia, but that the expression of the FGFR, flg, is lost from the same cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression of b-FGF and its receptor in rat brain during the process of neuronal death and repair after transient global cerebral ischemic injury.
the role of the FGF family of neurotrophic factors in the response to ischemic brain injury and in the subsequent process of neuronal cell repair and regeneration.
the role of the bFGF system in ischemic injury and repair.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the bFGF and FGF receptor system is involved in the ischemic injury and the repair of neurons.
bFGF and FGF receptor are expressed in a time dependent manner after ischemia and that the expression of these molecules are involved in the process of cell death and wound repair.

bFGF and FGFR are induced rapidly and dramatically by transient global ischemia in both neurons and glia, but that the translation of bFGF message is impaired during the period when ischemic neurons die.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
bFGF is an early and transient response gene in neurons, and a late and long-lasting response gene in glial cells.
bFGF and FGF receptors play a role in the ischemic process and that the changes in expression are complex and dynamic.
bFGF and FGFR are expressed by neurons in a region specific manner and are induced by ischemia in a region specific and time dependent manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
bFGF and FGFR expression are dynamic during the course of ischemic brain injury.

the expression of b-FGF and the FGFR is dynamically regulated in the hippocampus following ischemia, and that this dynamic expression pattern is not simply a reflection of the loss of pyramidal neurons, but also a response to the ischemic injury.
bFGF and FGF receptor are involved in neuronal cell death and wound repair response.
